The Fedwire Funds Service is the connection in scope for FHLB Cincinnati. More on ACI Connetic is at www.aciworldwide.com/solutions/payments-hub.

Federal Home Loan Bank of Cincinnati Moves Member Payment Processing to ACI Connetic
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 3:30 AM PDT 3 min read
FHLB Cincinnati teams will manage the payment operations on a platform ACI runs.
OMAHA, Neb., September 30, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ACI Worldwide (NASDAQ: ACIW), an original innovator in global payments technology, today announced that the Federal Home Loan Bank of Cincinnati (FHLB Cincinnati) is moving the payment processing behind its member funding services to ACI Connetic.
FHLB Cincinnati Advances outstanding grew in the first half of 2026. Funding a member Advance and taking a repayment both generate payment activity, and it has to be handled at whatever volume the day brings. Connetic will be delivered as a service. ACI operates the platform, and FHLB Cincinnati teams manage the payment operations that run on it.
"Our mission is to support our members and their communities by providing funding where and when needed with a high level of accuracy and reliability," said Andrew S. Howell, president and chief executive officer, FHLB Cincinnati. "Our partnership with Connetic allows our people to focus on servicing our members while having the confidence of strong connectivity to major payment networks and clearing systems."
ACI Connetic supports connectivity to major payment networks and clearing systems from a single platform, and each institution determines which connections its own implementation includes. The Fedwire Funds Service is the connection in scope for FHLB Cincinnati. More on ACI Connetic is at www.aciworldwide.com/solutions/payments-hub.
"Advance volume moves with what members need, and the payment behind it has to work every time. Connetic will give FHLB Cincinnati the ability to continue offering reliable payments in an efficient way with industry-leading technology," said Scotty Perkins, executive vice president, product management, payment software, ACI Worldwide. "Our job is the platform. Theirs is the payments, and the members waiting on them."
FHLB Cincinnati is one of 11 district banks in the Federal Home Loan Bank System, chartered by Congress in 1932 to provide liquidity for housing finance. The System's district banks are government-chartered, member-owned and privately capitalized, and together serve roughly 6,300 member financial institutions.
As of June 30, 2026, the FHLB is a AA+ rated wholesale cooperative bank owned by 588 member financial institutions, including banks, thrifts, credit unions, insurance companies and community development financial institutions in Kentucky, Ohio and Tennessee. The FHLB provides members access to products and services (primarily Advances, which are a readily available, low-cost source of funds, purchases of certain mortgage loans from members, and issuance of Letters of Credit to members) and a competitive return through quarterly dividends on their capital investment in the FHLB. The FHLB funds these products and services by raising private-sector capital from member-stockholders and, with the other Federal Home Loan Banks (FHLBanks) in the FHLBank System, issuing high-quality debt in the global capital markets. The FHLB also funds community investment programs that help its members create affordable housing and promote community economic development.

pages.title: ACI Worldwide adds Swift ledger routing to ACI Connetic
pages.text:
Credit: Piotr Swat / Shutterstock.com.
ACI Worldwide is extending ACI Connetic to support payments orchestrated through Swift’s ledger. The company said in a statement that the update brings “intelligent routing” for Swift ledger transactions into its cloud-native payments hub.
The capability is intended to help banks process tokenised deposit payments alongside traditional payment types under a single operating model.
The gold standard of business intelligence.
Experience unmatched clarity with a single platform that combines unique data, AI, and human expertise.
ACI said this approach uses existing operational controls, workflows and infrastructure, removing the need to run separate operations for digital-asset payment processing.
The update follows Swift’s announcement last year of a blockchain-based ledger. Swift has since said the ledger is ready for initial use, with 17 banks across six continents piloting use cases.
The ledger is designed to enable cross-border movement of tokenised deposits beyond a single institution and outside traditional operating hours.
ACI said many institutions are “yet to fit these payments into day-to-day operations”. It added ACI Connetic is intended to place Swift ledger transactions into the “same environment” that banks use to route, monitor, control and reconcile payments.
ACI Worldwide Account-to-Account Payments head and SVP Craig Ramsey said: “Digital assets should extend a bank’s payment capabilities, not force it to build a second payment operation.
“Banks need a practical way to operationalise tokenised deposits at scale using the people, controls and processes they already trust.
“With ACI Connetic, payments orchestrated through Swift’s ledger can be managed alongside other payment flows within a common operational framework.”
ACI Connetic is positioned as a platform that unifies payment types, payment rails and operational controls. Banks can use a single integration to originate, route and manage tokenised deposit payments and traditional payment flows.
The platform applies bank- and customer-defined rules to select clearing and settlement paths. ACI said this lets banks balance speed, cost, availability and customer expectations, while maintaining controls and visibility across the payment lifecycle.
Separately, ACI Worldwide earlier this year partnered with dLocal to provide global merchants with access to local payment methods in Brazil and Mexico.
